english: Father Sky and Mother Earth begot two sons. One was Twin, the other was the first man. Twin died; the man lived. He ploughed the field and sowed grain. He took a wife and begot children. The free people sprang from his children. Mortals are the descendants of the first man. When they are dead, they go to the brother of their own begetter. He received the dead in his house.
uncertain: bʰréh₂term̥ read as accusative of goal 'to the brother'
only the pie field was printed; no English seen

english: The dead man came to the house of the dead. Two old men stood at the door. Their heads (hair?) were white. They asked: Who are you? Whose son are you? I am the offspring of Earth and Sky. I am thirsty; give me water. Do not give me the water of that river. Whoever drinks it forgets his own lineage. The two gave him a drink from the other river. Then he remembered his lineage. He entered among the heroes.

Twin and his brother stood together. There was no sea and there was no sky. Then the brother struck him with a knife. From his flesh he fashioned the earth, and from his bones the stones; from his blood the water, and from his eyes the sun; from his skull the sky, and from his breath the wind; from his mind the moon, and from his mouth the fire. The earth is Twin's body. When a mortal dies, his bones go to the stones and his breath flies to the wind.

Two men met between the war-bands. The elder asked: Who is your father? The young man answered: My father is Of-Famous-Race. He went away and left me, a child, at home. He, being dead, does not come back. The old man recognized him and said: I am your father. The young man answered: Old man, you deceive me. Then the two hurled spears. They fought, and the spear of Of-Famous-Race struck the young man. Of-Famous-Race lamented his own son, the slain one. Then the lineage of Of-Famous-Race perished.
uncertain: só mr̥twós ne néseti: 'he is dead and does not return'?

english: No son was born to Good-Words; his child was a daughter. Good-Words said: Who will pour water for me when I am dead? He gave his daughter to Swift-Minded and said: Her boy will be my son. A boy was born to her; Good-Words lifted him up and gave him a name. You are my son and grandson. And so the lineage of Good-Words did not perish.
uncertain: ǵʰéwete looks 2pl, not 3sg 'who will pour' — read as 3sg

english: Two dogs guard the abode of the dead. They are Twin's two dogs. Their eyes are red and their teeth white. They go about among men. Whom death has seized, him they seek. They lead him to the abode of the dead. O dead man, run past the two dogs! Do not fear them. Throw them grain and honey, and they will let you pass. Go to the elders in the good abode. Your dear ones are there waiting.
uncertain: h₁usúh₁ stóygʰoh₁ instrumental of goal 'to the good abode'?
